The related SB846 Load Shift Goal Report by the CEC expects that the State is starting with a 2022 baseline of only 3,100–3,600 MW of load shifting. The SB846 Load-Shift Goal Report defines three categories of currently co-existing load flexible resources: (1) load-modifying, which impact load-serving entity (LSE) forecasts and resource procurement requirements, most commonly through a form of time-varying rates like time-of-use (TOU) and hourly dynamic rates; (2) resource planning and procurement, also known as supply- side demand response (DR), which can help meet Resource Adequacy (RA) requirements through economic DR or reliability DR activated during emergency conditions; and (3) incremental and emergency, which increase resource availability during events that fall outside of standard planning practices but do not contribute to the RA requirements of LSEs. By resource category, California’s 7,000 MW goal is expected to be met by: (1) 3,000 MW of load- modifying resource (starting from a 2022 baseline of 657-1,037 MW with 620-1,000 MW tied to TOU rates, 30 MW tied to dynamic pricing, and 7 MW tied to load management programs); (2) 2,825 MW of resource planning and procurement (starting from a 2022 baseline of 1,620-1,775 MW); and (3) 1,175 MW of incremental and emergency resource (starting from a 2022 baseline of 1,175 MW). The SB846 Load-Shift Goal Report essentially assumes no change for 2030 from 2022 baseline levels for incremental and emergency resource, modest change for resource planning and procurement, and major change for the load-modifying resource. This reflects “growth of loads under TOU rates such as electric vehicles and the policy preference for dynamic pricing-based load flexibility over event-based flexibility.” (Neumann and Lyon 2023). 72 The policy preference for dynamic pricing-based load flexibility is reflected in other actions described in Table A1. The first two of the four actions attributed to the CEC in Table A1 are most relevant and are related to each other: (1) the August 2021 public introduction of the pilot Market Informed Demand Automation Server (MIDAS); and (2) the 2022 amendments to the CEC’s Load Management Standards (2022 LMS).
